claim: A higher attack rate is a more aggressive attacker (according to Pendleton et al.).
quote: Another related attack rate metric measures the number of attacks that arrive at a system of interest per unit time [Zhan et al. 2013; Zhan et al. 2015]. Th ese metrics reﬂect the aggressiveness of cyber attacks.
locator: arXiv 1601.05792v1 p. A:15 (PDF p. 15), Sec. 5.1; ABSENT from the published ACM CSUR 49(4) version the bib cites, whose Sec. 7.1.1, p. 62:21 (PDF p. 21) keeps only the cybersecurity posture metric
issue: The cited published version contains no attack-rate sentence (and does not list Zhan 2013); only the arXiv v1 preprint, a different author list and title, has it. Even there it is (i) secondary, reporting Zhan et al. 2013/2015, and (ii) about attacks arriving at a target from all attackers reflecting the aggressiveness of cyber attacks, not one attacker's rate marking that attacker as aggressive.
fix_text: Either cite the arXiv v1 (new bib entry) or drop pendleton2016 and mark the reading as ours: "A higher attack rate is a more aggressive attacker \citep{pendleton2016}" -> "We read a higher attack rate as a more aggressive attacker". zhan2013 itself does not use 'aggressive'.
